cards.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, is writing to God's people scattered across five regions (1 Peter 1:1). He's already told them the old crowd heaps abuse on them for not joining in the wild life anymore (1 Peter 4:4). Now he calls them 'Beloved' and names what they're going through: a fiery trial.

cards.question: Peter tells these believers to treat their fiery trial as something strange and unexpected.
Instead of being surprised by the fiery trial, Peter tells them to ___.
Peter tells these believers to rejoice in their fiery trial. What reason does he give?

answers.text: Their trial proves their own strength
Their enemies will soon give up

cards.text: And sharing now leads somewhere: being OVERJOYED when His glory is revealed, and friend, with this much mustache I'm not sure anybody could even tell when I'm overjoyed. Then Peter gets specific about one kind of suffering, being insulted for the name of Christ.

cards.question: Peter says a believer who is insulted for the name of Christ is blessed.
Why does Peter call the believer who is insulted for Christ's name blessed?

answers.text: The Spirit of glory rests on them
The angels of heaven guard them
Their insulters will be struck down

cards.text: Now Peter draws a line: none of them should suffer as a murderer, a thief, a wrongdoer, or even a meddler. MEDDLER made the same list as MURDERER, friend, and I stick my mustache into every mixing bowl in this bakery, so I'm feeling REAL called out.

cards.question: But if they suffer as a Christian, Peter says not to be ___, and to glorify God that they bear that name.

cards.text: Then Peter keeps going, and I'll be honest, friend, the second I hear the word judgment my apron strings get tight. It's time, he says, for judgment to begin.

cards.question: Peter says judgment begins with the ___ of God.
If judgment begins with God's family, what does Peter ask next?

answers.text: What awaits those who disobey the gospel
How long the judgment will last
Who will stand as the judge

cards.text: Then Peter adds a quote, and friend, I read it once, put the dough down, and read it AGAIN with both eyebrows up: "If it is hard for the righteous to be saved, what will become of the ungodly and the sinner?"

cards.question: In the quote Peter adds, the ungodly and the sinner have an easier road than the righteous.

cards.text: So then, friend. I'm leaning in like it's the last ten seconds on my oven timer, because here comes Peter's word for everyone who suffers according to God's will.

cards.question: What does Peter say those who suffer according to God's will should do with their souls?

answers.text: Entrust them to their faithful Creator

cards.question: Peter says those who suffer according to God's will should stop doing good until the trial is over.

findings.problem: The pronoun "them" depends on earlier cards to identify Peter's audience. When this question appears by itself, it does not say who Peter is addressing; identify them as the believers in the question.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The pronoun "they" has no antecedent within the question and relies on earlier cards to identify Peter's readers. Make the question self-contained by naming the believers or using "a believer."
